title: NEET UG — Zoology | Phylum Coelenterata Cnidaria
description: Subject-wise test on Phylum Coelenterata Cnidaria (Zoology) for NEET UG. 40Q.
subject: neet-zoology
instructions: Section B: Attempt any 10 out of 15 questions
Correct answer: +4 marks | Wrong answer: -1 mark

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of organisms belonging to Phylum Coelenterata?

options.explanation: The notochord is a feature of Phylum Chordata, not Coelenterata.

options.text: Radial symmetry and acoelomate body plan
options.explanation: Cnidarians exhibit radial symmetry and an acoelomate body plan, lacking a true coelom.
Coelenterates lack a closed circulatory system.
Metameric segmentation is a feature of phyla like Annelida or Arthropoda.

questions.explanation: Phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria) typically exhibits radial symmetry and an acoelomate body plan, lacking a true coelom. The notochord is a feature of Chordata, closed circulatory system is absent, and metamerism is seen in higher phyla like Annelida or Arthropoda.
questions.hint: Consider the body plan and symmetry of organisms in Phylum Coelenterata.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A marine organism has a sac-like body with a single opening surrounded by tentacles and stinging cells. The organism is most likely a member of:

options.explanation: Porifera lacks true tissues and stinging cells.
Cnidarians have tentacles with stinging cells (cnidocytes) and a sac-like body.
Echinodermata have a water vascular system, not stinging cells.
Annelida have segmented bodies and lack stinging cells.

questions.explanation: Cnidarians (e.g., jellyfish, sea anemones) have a sac-like body (gastrovascular cavity) with one opening and tentacles bearing cnidocytes (stinging cells). Porifera lacks true tissues, Echinodermata has a water vascular system, and Annelida has a segmented body.
questions.hint: Focus on the presence of stinging cells and sac-like body structure.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: In the life cycle of Obelia (a hydrozoan), the stage that is diploid and produces gametes is:

options.explanation: Planula is a diploid larva but does not produce gametes.
The medusa is the diploid, sexually reproducing stage in Obelia.
Polyps are mostly asexual and do not produce gametes.
Ephyra is a juvenile medusa and not the primary gamete-producing stage.

questions.explanation: In Obelia, the medusa stage is the adult, diploid, and sexually reproducing phase that produces gametes. The planula is a diploid larva, polyps are mostly asexual, and ephyra is a juvenile medusa.
questions.hint: Identify the sexually reproducing stage in the life cycle of Obelia.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of cnidarians are exclusively marine?

options.explanation: Hydra includes freshwater species, and Aurelia is marine.
Physalia (Portuguese man-of-war) and Metridium (sea anemone) are exclusively marine.
Both include freshwater species.
Hydra includes freshwater species, while sea anemones are typically marine.

questions.explanation: Physalia (Portuguese man-of-war) and Metridium (sea anemone) are exclusively marine. Hydra and Obelia include freshwater species. Note: While some sea anemones are marine, Hydra is not exclusively marine.
questions.hint: Consider the habitat preferences of the listed cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The stinging cells (cnidocytes) in cnidarians are primarily used for:

options.explanation: Digestion occurs in the gastrovascular cavity, not via cnidocytes.
Locomotion in cnidarians is achieved through other means, not cnidocytes.
Cnidocytes are used for defense and capturing prey.
Excretion in cnidarians occurs via diffusion, not through cnidocytes.

questions.explanation: Cnidocytes contain nematocysts, which are used for defense and capturing prey. Digestion occurs in the gastrovascular cavity, locomotion varies (e.g., jet propulsion in medusae), and excretion is via diffusion.
questions.hint: Consider the primary function of cnidocytes in cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Corals are primarily responsible for building coral reefs. Reason (R): Corals secrete calcium carbonate to form exoskeletons.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason is also true.

questions.explanation: Corals (class Anthozoa) secrete calcium carbonate to form reefs. The assertion and reason are both correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Evaluate the relationship between the assertion and the reason.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a class under Phylum Coelenterata?

options.explanation: Hydrozoa is a class under Phylum Coelenterata.
Scyphozoa is a class under Phylum Coelenterata.
Anthozoa is a class under Phylum Coelenterata.
Turbellaria is a class under Phylum Platyhelminthes, not Coelenterata.

questions.explanation: Turbellaria is a class under Phylum Platyhelminthes (flatworms). The three classes of Coelenterata are Hydrozoa (e.g., Hydra), Scyphozoa (jellyfish), and Anthozoa (corals and sea anemones).
questions.hint: Recall the classes under Phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria).
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The alternation of generations in cnidarians refers to:

options.text: Alternation between haploid and diploid phases in the life cycle
options.explanation: Cnidarians do not exhibit true alternation between haploid and diploid phases.

options.text: Alternation between asexual polyp stage and sexual medusa stage
options.explanation: This refers to metagenesis in cnidarians.

options.text: Alternation between freshwater and marine habitats
options.explanation: There is no such alternation in cnidarians.

options.text: Alternation between solitary and colonial forms
options.explanation: This is not the definition of alternation of generations in cnidarians.

questions.explanation: Cnidarians exhibit metagenesis, alternating between asexual polyp and sexual medusa stages in their life cycle. The diploid phase dominates; there is no true alternation of haploid/diploid generations.
questions.hint: Think about the life cycle stages of cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A student observes a transparent, umbrella-shaped jellyfish pulsating in seawater. The organism is most likely a member of:

options.explanation: Hydrozoa includes smaller medusae, not necessarily umbrella-shaped.
Scyphozoa includes umbrella-shaped jellyfish.
Anthozoa lacks a medusa stage.
Ctenophora are not cnidarians.

questions.explanation: Jellyfish with a prominent umbrella-shaped medusa are characteristic of Scyphozoa (class of true jellyfish). Hydrozoa includes smaller medusae (e.g., Obelia), Anthozoa lacks a medusa stage, and Ctenophora (comb jellies) are not cnidarians.
questions.hint: Identify the class of cnidarians based on the medusa shape.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: In cnidarians, the nerve net is:

options.explanation: Cnidarians lack a centralized brain.

options.text: A diffuse network of neurons without a central control
options.explanation: This describes the nerve net in cnidarians.

options.text: A sensory structure for detecting light
options.explanation: This is not the primary function of the nerve net.
The nerve net is not a muscular system.

questions.explanation: Cnidarians possess a nerve net—a diffuse, non-centralized nervous system that coordinates responses without a brain. This is a key feature of their simple nerve organization. Options A, C, and D describe structures not found in cnidarians.
questions.hint: Recall the nervous system organization in cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of organisms belonging to Phylum Cnidaria?

options.explanation: Cnidarians do not possess a notochord.

options.text: Radial symmetry in most adult forms
options.explanation: Cnidarians exhibit radial symmetry in their adult forms.

options.text: Presence of a closed circulatory system
options.explanation: Cnidarians lack a closed circulatory system.
Cnidarians do not exhibit metameric segmentation.

questions.explanation: Cnidarians, such as jellyfish and hydra, exhibit radial symmetry in their adult forms, making option B correct. They lack a notochord (A), closed circulatory system (C), and metameric segmentation (D).
questions.hint: Consider the body symmetry of Cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which class of Cnidaria includes organisms that are exclusively marine and exhibit a medusa stage as the dominant phase in their life cycle?

options.explanation: Hydrozoa include both freshwater and marine species and typically have a dominant polyp stage.
Scyphozoa are exclusively marine and have a dominant medusa stage.
Anthozoa are exclusively marine but lack a medusa stage entirely.
Cubozoa are marine but not exclusively dominant in the medusa stage.

questions.explanation: Scyphozoa (true jellyfish) are exclusively marine and have a dominant medusa stage, unlike Hydrozoa (which have freshwater species and a dominant polyp stage), Anthozoa (which are polyp-only), or Cubozoa (box jellyfish, which are less common and not exclusively medusa-dominant).
questions.hint: Consider the dominance of the medusa stage in different classes.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A student observes a marine organism with a bell-shaped body, tentacles, and a gastrovascular cavity. The organism is likely to belong to which phylum?

options.explanation: Porifera lack tentacles and a gastrovascular cavity.
Cnidarians have a bell-shaped body, tentacles, and a gastrovascular cavity.
Platyhelminthes do not have a bell-shaped body or medusa stage.
Annelida do not have a bell-shaped body or medusa stage.

questions.explanation: The described features (bell-shaped body, tentacles, gastrovascular cavity) are characteristic of Cnidarians like jellyfish or sea nettles. Porifera (A) lack tentacles and a gastrovascular cavity; Platyhelminthes (C) and Annelida (D) do not have a bell-shaped body or medusa stage.
questions.hint: Consider the defining features of Cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stage in the life cycle of Obelia, a typical hydrozoan?

options.explanation: Planula larva is a stage in the life cycle of Obelia.
Polyp is a stage in the life cycle of Obelia.
Ephyra is not a stage in the life cycle of Obelia.
Medusa is a stage in the life cycle of Obelia.

questions.explanation: The life cycle of Obelia includes the planula larva, polyp (both hydroid and gonangium), and medusa stages. The ephyra is a juvenile medusa stage seen in Scyphozoa (e.g., jellyfish), not in Obelia.
questions.hint: Review the life cycle stages of Obelia.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Assertion: Cnidarians possess specialized stinging cells called cnidocytes. Reason: These cells are used for capturing prey and defense.

options.text: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.explanation: The assertion and reason are both true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

options.text: Assertion is true, but the reason is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true.

options.text: Assertion is false, but the reason is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Cnidocytes are indeed specialized stinging cells in Cnidarians used for prey capture and defense. The assertion and reason are both true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Understand the function of cnidocytes in Cnidarians.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of organisms belong to the same class of Cnidaria?

options.explanation: Hydra is a hydrozoan, while Sea anemone is an anthozoan.
Both Aurelia and Physalia belong to the class Hydrozoa.
Both Coral and Sea fan are anthozoans.
Hydra is a hydrozoan, while Jellyfish is a scyphozoan.

questions.explanation: Aurelia and Physalia both belong to the class Hydrozoa. Hydra is also a hydrozoan, but Sea anemone (A) is an anthozoan, Coral and Sea fan (C) are anthozoans, and Jellyfish (D) is a scyphozoan.
questions.hint: Classify the organisms based on their characteristics.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A researcher is studying a Cnidarian that exhibits both polyp and medusa stages in its life cycle, with the polyp stage being dominant. The organism is most likely a member of:

options.explanation: Scyphozoa have a dominant medusa stage.
Anthozoa lack a medusa stage entirely.
Hydrozoa exhibit both polyp and medusa stages, with the polyp stage often being dominant.
Cubozoa have a dominant medusa stage.

questions.explanation: Hydrozoans, such as Obelia, exhibit both polyp and medusa stages, with the polyp stage often being dominant. Scyphozoans (A) have a dominant medusa stage, Anthozoans (B) lack a medusa stage entirely, and Cubozoans (D) have a dominant medusa stage.
questions.hint: Consider the dominance of the polyp stage in different classes.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique feature of the class Anthozoa within Phylum Cnidaria?

options.text: Presence of a velum in the medusa stage
options.explanation: Velum is a feature of hydrozoan medusae, not Anthozoa.

options.text: Absence of a medusa stage in the life cycle
options.explanation: Anthozoans lack a medusa stage in their life cycle.
Anthozoans are primarily marine.
Anthozoans lack a notochord.

questions.explanation: Anthozoans (e.g., corals, sea anemones) are unique among Cnidarians because they exist only as polyps and lack a medusa stage in their life cycle. They are primarily marine (C is incorrect), do not have a velum (A is incorrect for Anthozoa; velum is a feature of hydrozoan medusae), and lack a notochord (D).
questions.hint: What distinguishes Anthozoa from other classes in Cnidaria?
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: In the life cycle of a typical scyphozoan jellyfish, the planula larva develops into a sessile stage called:

options.explanation: Ephyra is a juvenile medusa stage, not the sessile stage.
Strobila is a later stage involving transverse fission.
Scyphistoma is the sessile polyp stage that develops from the planula larva.
Planuloid is not a recognized stage in the life cycle of scyphozoans.

questions.explanation: In scyphozoans, the planula larva settles and develops into a sessile polyp called a scyphistoma. The strobila (B) is a later stage where transverse fission occurs, and ephyra (A) is the juvenile medusa released from the strobila.
questions.hint: Review the stages in the life cycle of scyphozoan jellyfish.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A student is given two organisms: one is a hydra (Class Hydrozoa) and the other is a sea anemone (Class Anthozoa). Which of the following features would help distinguish the two?

options.explanation: Both Hydra and sea anemone have tentacles.
Both Hydra and sea anemone exhibit radial symmetry.

options.text: Presence of a medusa stage in the life cycle
options.explanation: Hydra has a medusa stage (though reduced), while sea anemones do not.
Both Hydra (freshwater) and sea anemone (marine) are primarily aquatic.

questions.explanation: Hydra (Hydrozoa) has a medusa stage in its life cycle (though reduced), while sea anemones (Anthozoa) do not have a medusa stage at all. Both have tentacles (A) and radial symmetry (B), and both are primarily marine (D), so these features do not distinguish them.
questions.hint: Compare the life cycle stages of Hydra and sea anemone.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The characteristic feature of the phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria) is the presence of:

options.explanation: Flame cells are part of the excretory system in Platyhelminthes.
Radial symmetry and nematocysts are characteristic features of Coelenterata (Cnidaria).
Cnidarians lack a closed circulatory system.
Metameric segmentation is a feature of Annelida and Arthropoda, not Cnidaria.

questions.explanation: Coelenterata (Cnidaria) shows radial symmetry and contains stinging cells called nematocysts, which are used for defense and capturing prey. Flame cells are found in Platyhelminthes, a closed circulatory system is absent in cnidarians, and metameric segmentation is a feature of Annelida and Arthropoda.
questions.hint: Nematocysts are unique to this phylum and are used for stinging.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following organisms belongs to the class Hydrozoa?

options.explanation: Sea anemones belong to the class Anthozoa.
Jellyfish belong to the class Scyphozoa.
Obelia is a colonial hydrozoan belonging to the class Hydrozoa.
Octopus belongs to the phylum Mollusca.

questions.explanation: Obelia is a colonial hydrozoan belonging to the class Hydrozoa. Sea anemones belong to Anthozoa, jellyfish to Scyphozoa, and octopus to Mollusca.
questions.hint: Obelia is a classic example of a hydrozoan.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The body form of an organism in the phylum Coelenterata that is sessile and has a cylindrical body with a mouth surrounded by tentacles is called a:

options.explanation: Medusa is the free-swimming form in cnidarians.
Polyps are sessile, cylindrical forms with a mouth surrounded by tentacles.
Planula is a larval stage in cnidarians.
Ephyra is a juvenile medusa in Scyphozoa.

questions.explanation: Polyps are sessile, cylindrical forms with a mouth surrounded by tentacles, such as in Hydra. Medusa is the free-swimming form, planula is a larval stage, and ephyra is a juvenile medusa in Scyphozoa.
questions.hint: This form is typically attached to a substrate.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the cnidocytes in Cnidaria?

options.explanation: Cnidocytes are used for defense.
Cnidocytes are used for capturing prey.
Cnidocytes do not aid in locomotion.
Cnidocytes can help in attachment to substratum.

questions.explanation: Cnidocytes (stinging cells) are primarily involved in defense, prey capture, and sometimes attachment, but they do not aid in locomotion. Locomotion in cnidarians is performed by muscular contractions or by floating (in medusae).
questions.hint: Cnidocytes are specialized for stinging and adhesion.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Organisms of the phylum Coelenterata show tissue-level organization. Reason (R): They lack true organs and organ systems.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both statements are correct, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Coelenterates exhibit tissue-level organization (e.g., epithelial and muscular tissues) but lack true organs and organ systems. Thus, both statements are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Tissue-level organization means they have specialized cells but no complex organs.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly represents a member of the class Scyphozoa and its characteristic feature?

options.explanation: Hydra is a solitary polyp of Hydrozoa.

options.text: Aurelia – Medusa is the dominant stage
options.explanation: In Scyphozoa, the medusa is the dominant stage.
Metridium is a solitary sea anemone (Anthozoa).
Physalia is a colonial hydrozoan in marine habitats.

questions.explanation: In Scyphozoa (e.g., Aurelia), the medusa is the dominant stage, whereas polyps are reduced. Hydra is a solitary polyp of Hydrozoa, Metridium is a solitary sea anemone (Anthozoa), and Physalia (Portuguese man-of-war) is a colonial hydrozoan in marine habitats.
questions.hint: Scyphozoa is known for its medusa stage dominance.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: In the life cycle of Obelia, the stage that follows the planula larva is the:

options.explanation: The medusa is produced asexually from the polyp.
The planula larva settles and develops into a polyp.
Ephyra is a juvenile medusa in Scyphozoa.
Planula is the larval stage itself.

questions.explanation: The planula larva settles and develops into a polyp (the hydroid stage) in the life cycle of Obelia. The medusa is produced asexually from the polyp, and ephyra is a juvenile medusa in Scyphozoa.
questions.hint: The planula larva is a free-swimming stage that settles and transforms.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following features is shared by both Cnidaria and Ctenophora?

options.explanation: Nematocysts are unique to Cnidaria.
Both Cnidaria and Ctenophora exhibit radial symmetry.
Both are diploblastic.
Neither phylum has a closed circulatory system.

questions.explanation: Both Cnidaria and Ctenophora exhibit radial symmetry. Nematocysts are unique to Cnidaria, triploblastic organization is absent in both, and a closed circulatory system is not present in either.
questions.hint: Both phyla exhibit radial symmetry.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A student observes a marine organism with a transparent, umbrella-shaped body and trailing tentacles. This organism likely belongs to which class of Coelenterata?

options.explanation: Hydrozoa medusae are smaller and less prominent.
Anthozoa are exclusively polyps.
Scyphozoa includes true jellyfish with a transparent, umbrella-shaped body.
Cubozoa have cube-shaped medusae.

questions.explanation: The description matches a medusa, the dominant form in Scyphozoa (true jellyfish), which have a transparent, umbrella-shaped body. Hydrozoa medusae are smaller, Anthozoa are exclusively polyps, and Cubozoa have cube-shaped medusae.
questions.hint: The umbrella-shaped body is characteristic of jellyfish.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the phylum Coelenterata?

options.text: They exhibit both intracellular and extracellular digestion.
options.explanation: This statement is correct for Coelenterata.

options.text: They have a gastrovascular cavity with a single opening.
options.explanation: This statement is correct for Coelenterata.

options.text: They possess a well-developed brain and nervous system.
options.explanation: Coelenterates lack a brain and have a simple nerve net.

options.text: They reproduce both sexually and asexually.
options.explanation: This statement is correct for Coelenterata.

questions.explanation: Coelenterates lack a brain or centralized nervous system. They have a nerve net for coordination. The other options correctly describe their digestive and reproductive features.
questions.hint: Coelenterates have a simple nervous system, not a well-developed brain.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of organisms belonging to Phylum Coelenterata?

options.explanation: Notochord is a feature of chordates, not coelenterates.
Coelenterates exhibit radial symmetry and have a diploblastic body plan.
Jointed appendages are found in arthropods, not coelenterates.
Metameric segmentation is a feature of annelids and arthropods, not coelenterates.

questions.explanation: Coelenterates (Phylum Cnidaria) are characterized by radial symmetry and a diploblastic body organization (ectoderm and endoderm with mesoglea in between). They lack a notochord, jointed appendages, and metamerism.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which class of Coelenterata includes organisms that exhibit both polyp and medusa forms during their life cycle?

options.explanation: Hydrozoans exhibit both forms, but the question asks for a class that includes organisms with both forms.
Scyphozoans also exhibit both forms, but the question asks for a class that includes organisms with both forms.
Anthozoans exist only in the polyp form.
Both Hydrozoa and Scyphozoa include organisms that exhibit both polyp and medusa forms.

questions.explanation: Organisms in Hydrozoa (e.g., Hydra) and Scyphozoa (e.g., jellyfish) exhibit alternation of generations between polyp and medusa forms, while Anthozoa (e.g., sea anemones) exist only in the polyp form.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A student observes a marine organism with a bell-shaped body and tentacles. It exhibits bioluminescence and is commonly known as a 'box jellyfish.' To which class does this organism belong?

options.explanation: Hydrozoans are not box jellyfish.
Scyphozoans are typical jellyfish, not box jellyfish.
Box jellyfish belong to the class Cubozoa.
Anthozoans are sea anemones or corals, not box jellyfish.

questions.explanation: Box jellyfish belong to the class Cubozoa due to their cube-shaped bell and potent venom. They differ from typical jellyfish (Scyphozoa) in morphology and behavior.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the nervous system of Coelenterata?

options.text: They possess a nerve net without a central nervous system.
options.explanation: This statement is correct as coelenterates lack a central nervous system.

options.text: Nerve cells are distributed throughout the body.
options.explanation: This statement is correct as coelenterates have a nerve net.

options.text: There is no brain or ganglia present.
options.explanation: This statement is correct as coelenterates lack a brain or ganglia.

options.text: The nerve net coordinates movement and feeding.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because the question asks for an incorrect statement, and this one is correct.

questions.explanation: While Coelenterates have a nerve net, statement A is incorrect because they do not have a central nervous system like higher animals. All other statements correctly describe their nervous system.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: The stinging cells (nematocysts) in Coelenterata are primarily used for:

options.explanation: Nematocysts are not used for respiration.
Nematocysts are not used for digestion.
Nematocysts are primarily used for defense and capturing prey.
Nematocysts are not used for locomotion.

questions.explanation: Nematocysts are specialized stinging cells used by Coelenterates for defense and capturing prey. They contain venom to immobilize or kill small organisms.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a colonial coelenterate?

options.explanation: Hydra is a solitary coelenterate.
Obelia is a colonial coelenterate.
Sea anemones are solitary.
Physalia is a floating colony but not a typical colonial coelenterate like Obelia.

questions.explanation: Obelia is a colonial hydrozoan with interconnected polyps (gastrozooids and gonozooids). Hydra is solitary, while Physalia (Portuguese man-of-war) is a floating colony of modified polyps and medusae.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Corals are exclusively found in the class Anthozoa. Reason (R): Corals exhibit only the polyp form and lack a medusa stage. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is incorrect as R does explain A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Corals belong to Anthozoa and exist only as polyps, without a medusa stage. Thus, both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?

options.explanation: Hydra is correctly matched.
Aurelia is correctly matched.
Physalia is incorrectly matched as it is colonial.
Metridium is correctly matched.

questions.explanation: Physalia (Portuguese man-of-war) is a colonial coelenterate, not solitary. All other pairs are correctly matched.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: A researcher collects a sample from a coral reef and observes the following features: calcareous exoskeleton, polyp form only, and radial symmetry. The organism likely belongs to which class?

options.explanation: Hydrozoans lack a calcareous exoskeleton.
Scyphozoans are jellyfish-like and lack a calcareous exoskeleton.
Anthozoans, such as corals, have a calcareous exoskeleton and exist only as polyps.
Cubozoans lack a calcareous exoskeleton.

questions.explanation: Corals have a calcareous exoskeleton, exist only as polyps, and exhibit radial symmetry. These features are characteristic of the class Anthozoa.
questions.subject: neet-zoology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the coelenteron (gastrovascular cavity) in Coelenterata?

options.explanation: The coelenteron is involved in digestion.
The coelenteron circulates nutrients.
Respiration does not occur in the coelenteron.
The coelenteron eliminates waste.

questions.explanation: The coelenteron serves as a digestive cavity and circulates nutrients, but respiration occurs through the body surface. Waste elimination also occurs via the coelenteron.
questions.subject: neet-zoology
